text.tspan: A throw unwinds the stack until it meets a catch. Frames in between just disappear.
On success, on throw, even on an early return.
Use it to close, unlock, or hide a spinner,
Async errors need an async catch
The callback runs later, on an empty
stack: the try block is long gone.
await resumes inside the try, so a rejected
Always throw an Error, never a string; only an Error carries a stack. Catch where you can actually DO something;
letting it travel up is usually right. And a last line of defense: window.onerror plus window.onunhandledrejection.
